# The Reich Citizenship Law (15 September 1935) and First Regulation (14 November 1935)

## Bibliographic identity and selected witness

The selected witness is German History in Documents and Images, document1523, a three-page English PDF. Its credit identifies Nuremberg staff translation, edited by GHI staff, from Nazi Conspiracy and Aggression, volumeIV (Washington, DC: US Government Printing Office,1946), documents1416-PS and1417-PS, pp7–10. GHI separately identifies the German originals in Reichsgesetzblatt1935I, p1146ff and p1333. Those German originals and the1946 volume have not been independently collated in this admission.

## Reading scope and consumption

Two complete instruments in the GHI English translation; three PDF pages including source credits. No German facsimile collation. Editorial introduction remains distinct from statutory text. Full named scope was read in the T21 law development; the text hash matches the later T22 consumer-source receipt. This admission reuses that reading and rechecks the exact passages, not a new whole-book or archival investigation. No direct quotation is admitted.

The [language–law–nation history](../../../../histories/places-and-peoples/language-law-nation-centralisation/DEVELOPMENT.md#branch-vii-germany) consumes the bounded witness in its existing situated branch. Historical claim, legal prescription, authorial comparison and implementation evidence retain separate standing.

<a id="reich-1935-citizenship-law-first-regulation-q001"></a>
## Passage card — `reich-1935-citizenship-law-first-regulation-q001` — Citizenship and political standing
^reich-1935-citizenship-law-first-regulation-q001

> **Paraphrase (not a quotation):** The law distinguishes state subjecthood from Reich citizenship. It reserves citizenship to a subject classified as German or kindred blood who meets its conduct requirement; only Reich citizens receive full political rights. The implementing office is empowered to issue legal and administrative decrees. This records the statute’s racialising categories, not valid biological classifications or cancellation of every form of nationality.

- **Locator:** PDF pp1–2, instrumentI, §§1–3,15September1935.
- **Status:** paraphrase-only.
- **Source relation:** Paraphrased.
- **Verification:** exact named scope read in the prior law packet; saved witness and extraction hashes rebound2026-09-08.
- **Provenance:** institutional witness and immutable local-copy hashes above.
- **Use boundary:** Two complete instruments in the GHI English translation; three PDF pages including source credits. No German facsimile collation. Editorial introduction remains distinct from statutory text.

<a id="reich-1935-citizenship-law-first-regulation-q002"></a>
## Passage card — `reich-1935-citizenship-law-first-regulation-q002` — Classification and implementing authority
^reich-1935-citizenship-law-first-regulation-q002

> **Paraphrase (not a quotation):** The regulation assigns provisional citizenship and administrative withdrawal, defines classifications through ancestry and Jewish religious-community membership, and states further conditions for persons assigned two Jewish grandparents. It excludes persons classified as Jews from Reich citizenship, political voting and public office, while specifying transition, pension and other exceptions. Sections6–7 retain additional classification rules and exemption authority. The English legal prescription does not establish enforcement in every case.

- **Locator:** PDF pp2–3, instrumentII, §§1–7,14November1935; particular use §§2–5.
- **Status:** paraphrase-only.
- **Source relation:** Paraphrased.
- **Verification:** exact named scope read in the prior law packet; saved witness and extraction hashes rebound2026-09-08.
- **Provenance:** institutional witness and immutable local-copy hashes above.
- **Use boundary:** Two complete instruments in the GHI English translation; three PDF pages including source credits. No German facsimile collation. Editorial introduction remains distinct from statutory text.
